subject: Cognitive Science
title: Gestalt Principles
description: A quick win: understand Gestalt Principles.

hook.text: Look at three dots in a row and you see a line. Four dots in a square and you see a shape. Your brain groups automatically.

buildup.text: Gestalt psychologists identified laws of grouping: proximity, similarity, continuity, closure, and common fate.

discovery.text: These rules explain why you see constellations in random stars and faces in electrical outlets.

twist.text: 'The whole is different from the sum of its parts.' Gestalt isn't about pieces—it's about the patterns that emerge.

climax.text: Designers use Gestalt daily. Why a logo feels unified or a webpage feels cluttered comes down to these ancient rules.

punchline.text: Your brain sees patterns before it sees parts.

quiz.question: What do Gestalt principles describe?
options: How the brain groups sensory elements into patterns
